To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a common structural antigen is shared by all members of the simian papovavirus subgroup.

a common antigenic site is present on the major capsid protein of all polyoma and SV40 subgroup viruses and that the antigenic site is located in the carboxy-terminal half of the major capsid proteins of polyoma and SV 40 viruses.

the major capsid protein of polyoma virus is antigenically related to the major capsids protein of SV40 and that the relatedness of the major capsid proteins of polyoma and SV40 extends to other members of the polyomavirus subgroup.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the detection and identification of viruses in clinical material by immunofluorecence techniques.
the structural similarities between polyoma and SV40 viruses.
the identification of a common antigenic determinate located on the major capsid structural polypeptide of the polyoma virus-SV40 subgroup.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major capsid proteins of all members of the papovavirus SV40-polyoma sub-group share a common antigen.

the antigenic determinants on the major capsid protein of the simian papovaviruses are not species specific, but are common to the simian virus SV40 and polyoma viruses, and possibly to BK virus and other papovaviruses.
the antigenic determinant common in the major capsid proteins of SV40, polyoma, BK, rabbit vacuolating, and stumptailed macaca virus is a common structural antigen of the papovaviruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a common antigenic determinate between the major capsid protein of SV40 and the other polyomaviruses.
the common structural antigen (CSA) of the SV40 subgroup is a determinant of VP1, the major capsid protein of SV40.
all members of this subgroup share a common structural antigen located in their VP1 polypeptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the common antigenic determinant is located in the VP1 polypeptide of the simian viruses.
the common antigenic determinant is a major capsid polypetide.
the common antigenic determinant is not located on the VP2 polypeptide.
